section: Science · Ch42 — Force, Motion, Work & Energy
subject: Science
stem: When a moving bus suddenly stops, standing passengers tend to fall forward. This is best explained by:

options.option_text: Newton's First Law of Motion (inertia) — the body continues in motion even as the bus stops
Newton's Third Law of Motion only
The law of conservation of momentum applied to the passenger alone

explanation: Inertia (Newton's First Law) means a body in motion tends to stay in motion; when the bus stops suddenly, the passenger's body continues moving forward until an external force (friction, holding on) stops it.

section: Science · Ch42 — Force, Motion, Work & Energy
subject: Science
stem: A swimmer pushes water backward with their hands and moves forward. This illustrates:

options.option_text: Newton's Third Law — for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction

explanation: The swimmer's backward push on water (action) is met by an equal, opposite forward push of water on the swimmer (reaction) — a classic Third Law example.

section: Science · Ch42 — Force, Motion, Work & Energy
subject: Science
stem: The key difference between speed and velocity is that:

options.option_text: Velocity is speed with a specified direction; speed is only the magnitude
Speed and velocity are exactly the same with no difference
Velocity has no units, unlike speed
Speed can be negative, but velocity cannot

explanation: Speed is a scalar (magnitude only); velocity is a vector (magnitude plus direction) — a car going 60 km/h has a speed, but its velocity also specifies which way it's heading.
